Urshanabi.fact: His name is considered unusual and difficult to interpret, and consists of a prefix common in Sumerian names and a cuneiform numeral which could be read as either 2⁄3 or 40.

Urshanabi.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Urshanabi.question: He is known from the _____ and Standard Babylonian versions of the Epic of Gilgamesh, as well as from its Hittite adaptation
Urshanabi.fact: He is known from the Old Babylonian and Standard Babylonian versions of the Epic of Gilgamesh, as well as from its Hittite adaptation.

Urshanabi.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Urshanabi.question: He is described as a boatman in the service of the flood hero _____, and is responsible for taking Gilgamesh to Utnapishtim's domain
Urshanabi.fact: He is described as a boatman in the service of the flood hero Utnapishtim, and is responsible for taking Gilgamesh to Utnapishtim's domain.

Urshanabi.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Urshanabi.question: In the _____ version, he also subsequently travels with him back to Uruk
Urshanabi.fact: He is known from the Old Babylonian and Standard Babylonian versions of the Epic of Gilgamesh, as well as from its Hittite adaptation. In the Standard Babylonian version, he also subsequently travels with him back to Uruk.

Urshanabi.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Urshanabi.question: It has additionally been proposed that he might have been viewed as a survivor of the great flood, and that he acted as a ferryman of the dead comparable to Ḫumuṭ-tabal or _____
Urshanabi.fact: It has additionally been proposed that he might have been viewed as a survivor of the great flood, and that he acted as a ferryman of the dead comparable to Ḫumuṭ-tabal or Greek Charon.

Urshanabi.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Urshanabi.question: The first element, ur-, is common in _____ personal names and can be translated as “servant”
Urshanabi.fact: The first element, ur-, is common in Sumerian personal names and can be translated as “servant”. Gary Beckman notes this might have been the result of renewed interest in Sumerian language in the second half of the second millennium BCE.

Urshanabi.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Urshanabi.question: Gary Beckman notes this might have been the result of renewed interest in _____ language in the second half of the second millennium BCE
Urshanabi.fact: The first element, ur-, is common in Sumerian personal names and can be translated as “servant”. Gary Beckman notes this might have been the result of renewed interest in Sumerian language in the second half of the second millennium BCE.

Urshanabi.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Urshanabi.question: The convention of using numerals to represent names of deities is best attested from the _____ period, though older examples have been noted
Urshanabi.fact: The convention of using numerals to represent names of deities is best attested from the Middle Assyrian period, though older examples have been noted.

Urshanabi.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Urshanabi.question: However, _____ considers all of the proposed translations to be difficult to accept
Urshanabi.fact: However, Beckman considers all of the proposed translations to be difficult to accept.

Urshanabi.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Urshanabi.question: He is described as a boatman in the service of _____
Urshanabi.fact: His name is considered unusual and difficult to interpret, and consists of a prefix common in Sumerian names and a cuneiform numeral which could be read as either 2⁄3 or 40. Most likely it was an artificial scholarly construction.

Urshanabi.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Urshanabi.question: In the final section of the epic, he accompanies _____ back to Uruk
Urshanabi.fact: In the final section of the epic, he accompanies Gilgamesh back to Uruk. In the Standard Babylonian epic, Urshanabi is first mentioned by Shiduri when she explains to Gilgamesh how to reach Utanapishtim.

Urshanabi.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Urshanabi.question: The nature of the “_____” (šūt abni) is uncertain, and they have been variously interpreted as rudder oars, gunwales, punting poles, sails, anchor stones, kedges, talismans or anthropomorphic beings
Urshanabi.fact: Gilgamesh rushes there, armed with an axe and a dirk, and after encountering Urshanabi fights him and smashes the “Stone Ones” accompanying him. The nature of the “Stone Ones” (šūt abni) is uncertain, and they have been variously interpreted as rudder oars, gunwales, punting poles, sails, anchor stones, kedges, talismans or anthropomorphic beings.

Urshanabi.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Urshanabi.question: This section has been compared to similar recounting of _____’s deeds during his lament for Enkidu and during his meetings with Siduri and Utnapishitim
Urshanabi.fact: After a lacuna, Urshanabi asks Gilgamesh about his poor state, and in response hears the story of Enkidu’s death and realization of own mortality which followed it. This section has been compared to similar recounting of Gilgamesh’s deeds during his lament for Enkidu and during his meetings with Siduri and Utnapishitim.

Urshanabi.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Urshanabi.question: Each of the punting poles can only be used once, as it is the only way to guarantee _____ will not directly touch the potentially dangerous water
Urshanabi.fact: Gilgamesh subsequently demands to be taken to Utanapishtim, but Urshanabi informs him that since he smashed the “Stone Ones” the journey will be more difficult, and to solve the problem Gilgamesh needs to cut 300 poles to punt the boat, which he promptly does. Each of the punting poles can only be used once, as it is the only way to guarantee Gilgamesh will not directly touch the potentially dangerous water.

Urshanabi.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Urshanabi.question: The latter lacks a counterpart of the passage in which _____ recounts his deeds to the boatman
Urshanabi.fact: Since the initial encounter between Urshanabi and Gilgamesh is described on tablet X of the standard late edition of the epic, the Old Babylonian fragment preserving the same episode is sometimes called tablet X of the corresponding edition, but according to George this label should be avoided, as it is unknown how many tablets the older version of the epic had. The latter lacks a counterpart of the passage in which Gilgamesh recounts his deeds to the boatman.

Urshanabi.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Urshanabi.question: Utnapishtim curses him, presumably because he brought _____ to his home, and relieves him of his duties, possibly so that no mortal can reach the shore of his domain ever again
Urshanabi.fact: The latter lacks a counterpart of the passage in which Gilgamesh recounts his deeds to the boatman. Urshanabi appears again on tablet XI, after Gilgamesh fails to fulfill Utnapishtim’s request to remain awake for a week.

Urshanabi.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Urshanabi.question: When the hero returns, he informs him that he successfully obtained it, and that he will find out if it possesses the rejuvenating power attributed to it once he is back in _____
Urshanabi.fact: When the hero returns, he informs him that he successfully obtained it, and that he will find out if it possesses the rejuvenating power attributed to it once he is back in Uruk. The epic then concludes with Gilgamesh and Urshanabi returning to Uruk and Gilgamesh suggesting that Urshanabi should try climbing the city walls: It constitutes a repetition of a part of the first tablet of the epic, which similarly described Uruk, its walls, and important locations within it.

Urshanabi.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Urshanabi.question: Additionally, in a number of incantations _____ is addressed as a ferryman of the dead responsible for transporting them through the river Hubur
Urshanabi.fact: Additionally, in a number of incantations Gilgamesh is addressed as a ferryman of the dead responsible for transporting them through the river Hubur.

URU (Sumerogram).subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
URU (Sumerogram).question: It is commonly found in the intrigues of the 14th century BC _____ letters since the letters often concern city-state locations, or surrounding regions or cities/towns
URU (Sumerogram).fact: It is commonly found in the intrigues of the 14th century BC Amarna letters since the letters often concern city-state locations, or surrounding regions or cities/towns.

URU (Sumerogram).subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
URU (Sumerogram).question: URU is also used in the Epic of _____
URU (Sumerogram).fact: URU is also used in the Epic of Gilgamesh. The usage of URU in the Epic of Gilgamesh is only for Sumerogram "URU", (11 times).

URU (Sumerogram).subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
URU (Sumerogram).question: The usage of URU in the Epic of _____ is only for Sumerogram "URU", (11 times)
URU (Sumerogram).fact: URU is also used in the Epic of Gilgamesh. The usage of URU in the Epic of Gilgamesh is only for Sumerogram "URU", (11 times).

URU (Sumerogram).subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
URU (Sumerogram).question: The cuneiform sign is almost exclusively used as a _____ (capital letter (majuscule)), and in the Akkadian language, it is the Akkadian for "ālu", city, or town
URU (Sumerogram).fact: The cuneiform sign is almost exclusively used as a Sumerogram (capital letter (majuscule)), and in the Akkadian language, it is the Akkadian for "ālu", city, or town. The usage of URU in the Epic of Gilgamesh is only for Sumerogram "URU", (11 times).

URU (Sumerogram).subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
URU (Sumerogram).question: All uses in the Epic for URU are for various spellings of ālu, and usually an added sign complement; there is one usage in the Epic of URU for the city _____: URU.Šu-ri-ip-pak, (Tablet XI 11)
URU (Sumerogram).fact: All uses in the Epic for URU are for various spellings of ālu, and usually an added sign complement; there is one usage in the Epic of URU for the city Shuruppak: URU.Šu-ri-ip-pak, (Tablet XI 11).

Uruk.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Uruk.question: The _____ was Ancient city of Sumer and Babylonia.
Uruk.fact: Uruk, the archeological site known today as Warka, was an ancient city in the Near East or West Asia, located east of the current bed of the Euphrates River, on an ancient, now-dried channel of the river in Muthanna Governorate, Iraq. Uruk is the type site for the Uruk period and played a leading role in the early urbanization of Sumer in the mid-4th millennium BC.

Uruk.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Uruk.question: The site lies 93 kilometers (58 miles) northwest of ancient Ur, 108 kilometers (67 miles) southeast of ancient _____, and 24 kilometers (15 miles) northwest of ancient Larsa
Uruk.fact: The site lies 93 kilometers (58 miles) northwest of ancient Ur, 108 kilometers (67 miles) southeast of ancient Nippur, and 24 kilometers (15 miles) northwest of ancient Larsa.

Uruk.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Uruk.question: After the end of the _____ period, with the rise of the Akkadian Empire, the city lost its prime importance
Uruk.fact: After the end of the Early Dynastic period, with the rise of the Akkadian Empire, the city lost its prime importance.

Uruk.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Uruk.question: William Kennett Loftus visited the site of Uruk in _____, identifying it as "Erech", known as "the second city of Nimrod", and led the first excavations from 1850 to 1854
Uruk.fact: William Kennett Loftus visited the site of Uruk in 1849, identifying it as "Erech", called "the second city of Nimrod", and led the first excavations from 1850 to 1854.

Uruk.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Uruk.question: In Ancient Greek, it was known as Ὀρχόη (_____óē), Ὀρέχ (Orékh), and Ὠρύγεια (Ōrúgeia)
Uruk.fact: In Ancient Greek, it was called Ὀρχόη (Orkhóē), Ὀρέχ (Orékh), and Ὠρύγεια (Ōrúgeia).

Uruk.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Uruk.question: The temple complexes at their cores became the _____ (Unug) dedicated to Inanna and the "Anu" District of Kullaba
Uruk.fact: The temple complexes at their cores became the Eanna District (Unug) dedicated to Inanna and the "Anu" District of Kullaba. The Eanna District comprised several buildings with workshop spaces and was walled off from the city.

Uruk.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Uruk.question: By contrast, the _____ was built on a terrace with a temple at the top
Uruk.fact: By contrast, the Anu District was built on a terrace with a temple at the top.

Uruk.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Uruk.question: The rest of the city was composed of typical courtyard houses, grouped by profession of the occupants, in districts around _____ and Anu
Uruk.fact: The Eanna District comprised several buildings with workshop spaces and was walled off from the city. It is clear Eanna was dedicated to Inanna from the earliest Uruk period throughout the history of the city.

Uruk.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Uruk.question: This canal system flowed throughout the city connecting it with the maritime trade on the ancient _____ as well as the surrounding agricultural belt
Uruk.fact: This canal system flowed throughout the city connecting it with the maritime trade on the ancient Euphrates River as well as the surrounding agricultural belt. The original city of Uruk was situated southwest of the ancient Euphrates River.

Uruk.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Uruk.question: Today, the site of _____ is northeast of the river
Uruk.fact: Today, the site of Warka is northeast of the river.

Uruk.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Uruk.question: In _____, two different copies of an inscription were put forth as evidence of a 19th-century BC ruler of Uruk named Naram-sin
Uruk.fact: In 2009, two different copies of an inscription were put forth as evidence of a 19th-century BC ruler of Uruk named Naram-sin.

Uruk.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Uruk.question: _____ BC), Rîm-Anum and Nabi-ilīšu
Uruk.fact: 1740 BC), Rîm-Anum and Nabi-ilīšu.

Uruk.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Uruk.question: The Eanna District was restored as part of an ambitious building program, which included a new temple for _____
Uruk.fact: The Eanna District was restored as part of an ambitious building program, which included a new temple for Inanna.

Uruk.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Uruk.question: _____ BC), Uruk went into a steep decline until about 850 BC when the Neo-Assyrian Empire annexed it as a provincial capital
Uruk.fact: 2000 BC), Uruk went into a steep decline until about 850 BC when the Neo-Assyrian Empire annexed it as a provincial capital.

Uruk.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Uruk.question: The Bīt Reš along with the _____ was one of the two main centers of Neo-Babylonian astronomy
Uruk.fact: The Bīt Reš along with the Esagila was one of the two main centers of Neo-Babylonian astronomy.

Uruk.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Uruk.question: All of the temples and canals were restored again under _____
Uruk.fact: All of the temples and canals were restored again under Nabopolassar.

Uruk.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Uruk.question: In 200 BC, the '_____' (Cuneiform: E₂.IRI₁₂.GAL, Sumerian: eš-gal) of Ishtar was added between the Anu and Eanna districts
Uruk.fact: In 200 BC, the 'Great Sanctuary' (Cuneiform: E₂.IRI₁₂.GAL, Sumerian: eš-gal) of Ishtar was added between the Anu and Eanna districts.

Uruk.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Uruk.question: The ziggurat of the temple of Anu, which was rebuilt in this period, was the largest ever built in _____
Uruk.fact: The ziggurat of the temple of Anu, which was rebuilt in this period, was the largest ever built in Mesopotamia. When the Seleucids lost Mesopotamia to the Parthians in 141 BC, Uruk continued in use.

Uruk.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Uruk.question: As in the rest of _____, power moved progressively from the temple to the palace
Uruk.fact: This is pointed out repeatedly in the references to this city in religious and, especially, in literary texts, including those of mythological content; the historical tradition as preserved in the Sumerian king-list confirms it. As in the rest of Sumer, power moved progressively from the temple to the palace.

Uruk.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Uruk.question: Afterwards, kingship passed to Kish at the beginning of the _____ period, which corresponds to the beginning of the Early Bronze Age in Sumer
Uruk.fact: Rulers from the Early Dynastic period exercised control over Uruk and, at times, over all of Sumer. Afterwards, kingship passed to Kish at the beginning of the Early Dynastic period, which corresponds to the beginning of the Early Bronze Age in Sumer.

Uruk.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Uruk.question: This period is sometimes called the _____
Uruk.fact: This period is sometimes called the Golden Age.

Uruk.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Uruk.question: Much of _____ architecture can trace its roots to these prototypical buildings
Uruk.fact: Much of Near Eastern architecture can trace its roots to these prototypical buildings.

Uruk.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Uruk.question: The following table summarizes the significant architecture of the Eanna and _____
Uruk.fact: The following table summarizes the significant architecture of the Eanna and Anu Districts.

Uruk.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Uruk.question: Temple N, the Cone-_____, and the Round Pillar Hall are often referred to as a single structure: the Cone-Mosaic Temple
Uruk.fact: Temple N, the Cone-Mosaic Courtyard, and the Round Pillar Hall are often called a single structure: the Cone-Mosaic Temple.

Uruk.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Uruk.question: During the following _____ period it grew to a size of 600 ha (1,500 acres) by c
Uruk.fact: During the following Jemdet Nasr period it grew to a size of 600 ha (1,500 acres) by c.

Uruk.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Uruk.question: There are three major tells within the site: _____ district, Bit Resh (Kullaba), and Irigal
Uruk.fact: There are three major tells within the site: The Eanna district, Bit Resh (Kullaba), and Irigal.

Uruk.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Uruk.question: The location of Uruk was first noted by Fraser and Ross in _____
Uruk.fact: The location of Uruk was first noted by Fraser and Ross in 1835.

Uruk.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Uruk.question: William Loftus excavated there in _____ and 1854 after a scouting mission in 1849
Uruk.fact: William Loftus excavated there in 1850 and 1854 after a scouting mission in 1849.

Uruk.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Uruk.question: A large basalt stela found by _____ was later lost
Uruk.fact: William Loftus excavated there in 1850 and 1854 after a scouting mission in 1849. By Loftus' own account, he admits that the first excavations were superficial at best, as his financiers forced him to deliver large museum artifacts at a minimal cost.

Uruk.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Uruk.question: Warka was also scouted by archaeologist Walter Andrae in _____
Uruk.fact: Warka was also scouted by archaeologist Walter Andrae in 1902.

Uruk.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Uruk.question: In _____ Warka was visited by archaeologist Edgar James Banks
Uruk.fact: In 1905 Warka was visited by archaeologist Edgar James Banks.

Uruk.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Uruk.question: From _____ to 1913, Julius Jordan and his team from the German Oriental Society discovered the temple of Ishtar, one of four known temples located at the site
Uruk.fact: From 1912 to 1913, Julius Jordan and his team from the German Oriental Society discovered the temple of Ishtar, one of four known temples located at the site.

Uruk.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Uruk.question: The GOS returned to Uruk in _____ and excavated until 1939, when World War II intervened
Uruk.fact: The GOS returned to Uruk in 1928 and excavated until 1939, when World War II intervened.

Uruk.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Uruk.question: The team was led by Jordan until _____ when Jordan became Director of Antiquities in Baghdad, then by A. Nöldeke, Ernst Heinrich, and H. J. Lenzen
Uruk.fact: The team was led by Jordan until 1931 when Jordan became Director of Antiquities in Baghdad, then by A. Nöldeke, Ernst Heinrich, and H. J. Lenzen.

Uruk.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Uruk.question: The German excavations resumed after the war and were under the direction of Heinrich Lenzen from _____ to 1967
Uruk.fact: The German excavations resumed after the war and were under the direction of Heinrich Lenzen from 1954 to 1967.

Uruk.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Uruk.question: He was followed in _____ by J. Schmidt, and in 1978 by R.M. Boehmer
Uruk.fact: He was followed in 1968 by J. Schmidt, and in 1978 by R.M. Boehmer.

Uruk.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Uruk.question: This was followed up with high-resolution satellite imagery in _____
Uruk.fact: This was followed up with high-resolution satellite imagery in 2005.

Uruk.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Uruk.question: Work resumed in _____ and is currently concentrated on the city wall area and a survey of the surrounding landscape
Uruk.fact: Work resumed in 2016 and is currently concentrated on the city wall area and a survey of the surrounding landscape.

Uruk.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Uruk.question: Afterward 25 sediment cores, up to 13 meters deep, were done in _____ and 2025 and a virtual geophysical topology of the Uruk area was produced
Uruk.fact: Afterward 25 sediment cores, up to 13 meters deep, were done in 2024 and 2025 and a virtual geophysical topology of the Uruk area was produced.

Uruk.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Uruk.question: 3500 BC) "numerical tablets" or "impressed tablets", _____ were from the Uruk IV period (c
Uruk.fact: 3500 BC) "numerical tablets" or "impressed tablets", 1776 were from the Uruk IV period (c.

Uruk.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Uruk.question: 3200–2900 BC) which is also called the _____ period
Uruk.fact: 3200–2900 BC) which is also called the Jemdet Nasr period.

Uruk.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Uruk.question: Later cuneiform tablets were deciphered and include the famous SKL, a record of kings of the _____ civilization
Uruk.fact: Later cuneiform tablets were deciphered and include the famous SKL, a record of kings of the Sumerian civilization.

Uruk.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Uruk.question: Many of the cuneiform tablets form acquisitions by museums and collections as the British Museum, _____, and the Louvre
Uruk.fact: Many of the cuneiform tablets form acquisitions by museums and collections as the British Museum, Yale Babylonian Collection, and the Louvre.

Uruk.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Uruk.question: The carved marble female face is probably a depiction of _____
Uruk.fact: The carved marble female face is probably a depiction of Inanna.

Uruk.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Uruk.question: The mask was looted from the Iraq Museum during the invasion of Iraq in April _____
Uruk.fact: The mask was looted from the Iraq Museum during the invasion of Iraq in April 2003. It was recovered in September 2003 and returned to the museum.

Uruk.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Uruk.question: It was recovered in September _____ and returned to the museum
Uruk.fact: The mask was looted from the Iraq Museum during the invasion of Iraq in April 2003. It was recovered in September 2003 and returned to the museum.

Uruk.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Uruk.question: The structure of the _____ further develops some mythological concepts from Enuma Elish, perhaps involving libation rites as indicated from the channels, tanks, and vessels found there
Uruk.fact: The Stone Temple was built of limestone and bitumen on a podium of rammed earth and plastered with lime mortar. The structure of the Stone Temple further develops some mythological concepts from Enuma Elish, perhaps involving libation rites as indicated from the channels, tanks, and vessels found there.

Uruk.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Uruk.question: The combination of these two developments places _____ as arguably the first true city and civilization in human history
Uruk.fact: The combination of these two developments places Eanna as arguably the first true city and civilization in human history. Eanna during period IVa contains the earliest examples of writing.

Uruk.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Uruk.question: The first building of Eanna, Stone-_____ (Mosaic Temple), was built in period VI over a preexisting Ubaid temple and is enclosed by a limestone wall with an elaborate system of buttresses
Uruk.fact: The first building of Eanna, Stone-Cone Temple (Mosaic Temple), was built in period VI over a preexisting Ubaid temple and is enclosed by a limestone wall with an elaborate system of buttresses. The Stone-Cone Temple, named for the mosaic of colored stone cones driven into the adobe brick façade, may be the earliest water cult in Mesopotamia.

Uruk.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Uruk.question: However, the _____ was unprecedented for its size and use of stone, a clear departure from traditional Ubaid architecture
Uruk.fact: In the following period, Uruk V, about 100 m east of the Stone-Cone Temple the Limestone Temple was built on a 2 m high rammed-earth podium over a pre-existing Ubaid temple, which like the Stone-Cone Temple represents a continuation of Ubaid culture. However, the Limestone Temple was unprecedented for its size and use of stone, a clear departure from traditional Ubaid architecture.

Uruk.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Uruk.question: The Limestone Temple is probably the first _____ temple, but it is impossible to know with certainty
Uruk.fact: The Limestone Temple is probably the first Inanna temple, but it is impossible to know with certainty.

Uruk.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Uruk.question: Like the Stone-Cone temple the _____ temple was also covered in cone mosaics
Uruk.fact: It is unclear if the entire temple or just the foundation was built of this limestone. The Limestone Temple is probably the first Inanna temple, but it is impossible to know with certainty.

Uruk.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Uruk.question: Between these two monumental structures a complex of buildings (called A–C, E–K, _____, Cone-Mosaic), courts, and walls was built during Eanna IVb
Uruk.fact: Between these two monumental structures a complex of buildings (called A–C, E–K, Riemchen, Cone-Mosaic), courts, and walls was built during Eanna IVb. The Riemchen Building, named for the 16 cm (6.3 in)×16 cm (6.3 in) brick shape called Riemchen by the Germans, is a memorial with a ritual fire kept burning in the center for the Stone-Cone Temple after it was destroyed.

Uruk.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Uruk.question: The use of colored cones as a façade treatment was greatly developed as well, perhaps used to greatest effect in the Cone-_____
Uruk.fact: The use of colored cones as a façade treatment was greatly developed as well, perhaps used to greatest effect in the Cone-Mosaic Temple.

Uruk.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Uruk.question: Composed of three parts: Temple N, the _____, and the Cone-Mosaic Courtyard, this temple was the most monumental structure of Eanna at the time
Uruk.fact: Composed of three parts: Temple N, the Round Pillar Hall, and the Cone-Mosaic Courtyard, this temple was the most monumental structure of Eanna at the time.

Uruk.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Uruk.question: They were all ritually destroyed and the entire _____ district was rebuilt in period IVa at an even grander scale
Uruk.fact: The Riemchen bricks first used in this temple were used to construct all buildings of Uruk IV period Eanna. Composed of three parts: Temple N, the Round Pillar Hall, and the Cone-Mosaic Courtyard, this temple was the most monumental structure of Eanna at the time.

Uruk.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Uruk.question: During Eanna IVa, the _____ was demolished and the Red Temple built on its foundations
Uruk.fact: During Eanna IVa, the Limestone Temple was demolished and the Red Temple built on its foundations.

Uruk.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Uruk.question: Also in period IV, the _____, a sunken courtyard surrounded by two tiers of benches covered in cone mosaic, was built
Uruk.fact: Also in period IV, the Great Court, a sunken courtyard surrounded by two tiers of benches covered in cone mosaic, was built. A small aqueduct drains into the Great Courtyard, which may have irrigated a garden at one time.

Uruk.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
